Rebuild this interaction 1:1: Amie's search sheet - tapping the search icon slides a dark sheet up over the calendar revealing a "Todos, emails, meetings" field that immediately raises the system keyboard, cursor already blinking.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Dark calendar with a bottom panel (Inbox, Today, + Create list). Search state: a near-full-height dark sheet with a single rounded search field (magnifier icon, placeholder "Todos, emails, meetings") and the system keyboard docked below it.

## Motion spec
Pattern: one-shot search surface.
- Tap search: the sheet rises from the bottom panel (spring ~340/24, no bounce - utility, not play) while the calendar dims 50%.
- The search field fades in at the sheet's top edge (200ms, 80ms after the rise starts) and auto-focuses: the keyboard slides up with the system spring, arriving exactly as the sheet settles - one continuous upward motion.
- The cursor blinks in the field before the keyboard finishes arriving - input is never blocked.
- Typing filters results into the dimmed space above the keyboard; the field's magnifier pulses once on the first keystroke.
- Dismiss (swipe down or the X): keyboard and sheet drop together as one unit (spring ~360/26), the calendar un-dimming.

## Calibration
- Sheet and keyboard move as a coupled stack - no gap ever opens between them.
- Placeholder text lists the searchable domains - it's the whole feature pitch.

## Reduced motion
Sheet and keyboard appear without spring.

## Don't miss
- Auto-focus is the point: two surfaces (sheet, keyboard) but ONE tap from the user.
- The dismiss gesture anywhere on the dim works - search is a detour, not a destination.
